text: When designing REST APIs, it is important to follow some best practices. First, use clear and meaningful endpoints that represent your resources, such as /users or /orders. Second, always return the correct HTTP status codes so clients understand what happened. For example, use 200 for success, 404 when something is not found, and 500 for server errors. Third, write good documentation so other developers can learn how to use your API without difficulty. Finally, plan for versioning from the start. When you change your API in ways that could break existing clients, create a new version instead of changing the old one.
